title: Preserve existing plan as context when re-planning
description: When a plan review legitimately fails and the feature goes back to planning, the planner currently starts from scratch using only the title and description. Instead, pass the existing feature.plan into the planning prompt as a 'previous plan' section so the planner can refine it rather than rewrite from zero. This avoids losing good work when only part of the plan needs fixing. Requires adding a {previous_plan} variable to plan-headless.md and populating it in run_planning.
plan:
## Plan: Preserve Existing Plan as Context When Re-planning

### Overview
When a plan review fails and the feature moves back to planning, the planner currently starts from scratch using only the title and description. This loses good work when only part of the plan needs fixing. We'll modify the planning system to pass the existing plan as context so the planner can refine it rather than rewrite from zero.

### Key Changes

#### 1. Modify run_planning function (pipeline/phases.py:611)
- Add logic to detect when a feature has an existing plan (feature.plan is not empty)
- Create a previous_plan_context variable to pass to the template
- Add the previous_plan context to the prompt building, similar to how questions_context and feedback_context are currently handled

**Implementation details:**
```python
# After line 640 (where feedback_context is created), add:
previous_plan_context = ""
if feature.plan and feature.plan.strip():
    previous_plan_context = f"\n\n## Previous Plan (refine rather than rewrite):\n{feature.plan}\n"
```

#### 2. Update plan-headless.md template (pipeline/prompts/plan-headless.md)
- Add a {previous_plan} variable placeholder in the template
- Add instructions to tell the AI to refine the previous plan if one exists
- Position this after the description but before the main instructions

**Template addition:**
```markdown
{previous_plan}
```

#### 3. Update _build_prompt call in run_planning
- Add the {previous_plan} variable to the template substitution dictionary
- Append previous_plan_context to the prompt after template building, similar to questions_context and feedback_context

**Implementation:**
- Use the same pattern as questions_context and feedback_context - append after the main prompt is built
- This ensures the previous plan context is always included when present

### Technical Implementation Details

#### File Locations:
- **run_planning function:** pipeline/phases.py lines 611-721
- **Template file:** pipeline/prompts/plan-headless.md
- **_build_prompt function:** Used for variable substitution in template

#### Integration Points:
- The change plugs into the existing re-planning flow at line 1097 in phases.py where `run_planning(feature, runner, status=status)` is called after plan review failure
- Uses existing FeatureFile.plan property to access previous plan content
- Follows established pattern of conditional context sections (questions_context, feedback_context)

### Testing Strategy
1. Create a test feature with an initial plan
2. Have plan review fail and trigger re-planning
3. Verify that the previous plan is passed as context to the planner
4. Confirm that planner can refine the existing plan rather than starting fresh

### Expected Behavior
- When re-planning after review failure, the AI will see both the original description AND the previous plan
- The AI can build upon the good parts of the previous plan while addressing the specific feedback from the review
- This preserves valuable planning work and makes the iteration more efficient
- If no previous plan exists (first-time planning), behavior remains unchanged

# Implementation Spec: Preserve Existing Plan as Context When Re-planning

## Task 1: Add previous_plan_context logic to run_planning function
**File:** pipeline/phases.py
**Location:** Lines 611-721 (run_planning function)
**Dependencies:** None

### What to modify:
- Add previous_plan_context variable after line 640 (after feedback_context creation)
- Append previous_plan_context to prompt after template building (after line 654)

### Approach:
```python
# After line 640, add:
previous_plan_context = ""
if feature.plan and feature.plan.strip():
    previous_plan_context = f"\n\n## Previous Plan (refine rather than rewrite):\n{feature.plan}\n"

# After line 654 (after feedback_context append), add:
if previous_plan_context:
    prompt += previous_plan_context
```

### Technical details:
- Use the existing FeatureFile.plan property to access previous plan content
- Follow the same pattern as questions_context and feedback_context
- Only include context if plan exists and is not empty/whitespace
- Position after template building but before _run_phase call

## Task 2: Update plan-headless.md template with previous plan instructions
**File:** pipeline/prompts/plan-headless.md
**Location:** After description section (around line 4)
**Dependencies:** Task 1 must be completed first

### What to modify:
- Add {previous_plan} placeholder in the template
- Add instructions about refining existing plans vs starting fresh

### Approach:
```markdown
**Description:** {description}

{previous_plan}

---
```

### Technical details:
- Position the placeholder after description but before main instructions
- The placeholder will be replaced by _build_prompt if previous_plan_context is provided
- If no previous plan exists, the placeholder will remain empty

## Task 3: Add previous_plan to _build_prompt template substitution
**File:** pipeline/phases.py
**Location:** Lines 642-648 (template building call)
**Dependencies:** Task 2 must be completed first

### What to modify:
- Add {previous_plan} key to the replacements dictionary passed to _build_prompt

### Approach:
```python
prompt = _build_prompt(template, {
    "{title}": feature.title,
    "{description}": feature.get_section("Description") or "(no description)",
    "{feature_slug}": feature.slug,
    "{feature_id}": feature.id,
    "{phase}": "planning",
    "{previous_plan}": previous_plan_context,  # Add this line
}, "planning")
```

### Technical details:
- This ensures the {previous_plan} placeholder is properly substituted in the template
- If previous_plan_context is empty, the placeholder will be replaced with empty string
- Template substitution happens before additional context is appended

## Task 4: Create test to verify previous plan preservation
**File:** New test file or existing test suite
**Dependencies:** Tasks 1-3 must be completed

### What to create:
- Test that creates a feature with an initial plan
- Simulates plan review failure
- Verifies that re-planning includes the previous plan as context
- Confirms the previous plan appears in the planning prompt

### Approach:
1. Create test feature with plan content
2. Mock plan review failure to trigger re-planning
3. Capture the prompt sent to the planning agent
4. Assert that previous plan content appears in the prompt
5. Verify the format matches expected structure

### Technical details:
- Use existing test patterns from pipeline/test_*.py files
- Mock AgentRunner and capture prompt parameter to _run_phase
- Test both cases: with previous plan and without previous plan
- Ensure no regression in normal first-time planning flow

## Integration Points:

**Re-planning trigger:** The change integrates at line 1097 in phases.py where `run_planning(feature, runner, status=status)` is called after plan review failure.

**Data source:** Uses existing FeatureFile.plan property to access previous plan content.

**Pattern consistency:** Follows established pattern of conditional context sections (questions_context, feedback_context) that are appended after template building.

**Template system:** Uses existing _build_prompt function for variable substitution in templates.

## Expected Behavior Changes:

1. **With previous plan:** When re-planning after review failure, the AI sees both the original description AND the previous plan with instructions to refine rather than rewrite.

2. **Without previous plan:** First-time planning behavior remains unchanged - no previous plan context is added.

3. **Performance impact:** Minimal - only adds string concatenation and conditional logic to existing planning flow.

4. **Backward compatibility:** Fully backward compatible - existing features and templates continue to work unchanged.
test_spec:
# Test Specification: Preserve Existing Plan as Context When Re-planning

## 1. Behaviors That MUST Be Verified

### 1.1 Previous Plan Context Injection
**Behavior**: When a feature has an existing plan and enters re-planning phase, the previous plan should be included as context.
**Success Criteria**: 
- previous_plan_context variable is populated with existing feature.plan content
- Context includes header "## Previous Plan (refine rather than rewrite):"
- Previous plan content is properly formatted and escaped
**Expected Output**: Context string containing formatted previous plan

### 1.2 Empty Plan Handling
**Behavior**: When a feature has no existing plan (first-time planning), no previous plan context should be added.
**Success Criteria**:
- previous_plan_context remains empty string when feature.plan is None or empty
- No "Previous Plan" section appears in prompt
- Planning proceeds normally without previous context
**Expected Output**: Empty previous_plan_context variable

### 1.3 Template Variable Substitution
**Behavior**: The {previous_plan} placeholder in plan-headless.md template should be replaced with previous plan context.
**Success Criteria**:
- Template contains {previous_plan} placeholder
- _build_prompt correctly substitutes the variable
- Final prompt includes previous plan section when applicable
**Expected Output**: Fully rendered template with previous plan context inserted

### 1.4 Prompt Building Integration
**Behavior**: Previous plan context should be appended to the final prompt similar to questions_context and feedback_context.
**Success Criteria**:
- Context is appended after template building
- Follows same pattern as existing context sections
- Order is maintained: base template + questions + feedback + previous plan
**Expected Output**: Complete prompt with all context sections properly ordered

### 1.5 Re-planning Trigger Integration
**Behavior**: When plan review fails and triggers re-planning at phases.py:1097, the previous plan should be available as context.
**Success Criteria**:
- run_planning function receives feature with existing plan data
- Previous plan is extracted and formatted before prompt building
- Context flows through to AI planner request
**Expected Output**: AI receives both original description AND previous plan content

### 1.6 Plan Content Preservation
**Behavior**: Original plan content should be preserved exactly as stored, without modification or truncation.
**Success Criteria**:
- No text transformation or sanitization of plan content
- Whitespace, formatting, and special characters preserved
- Complete plan content included regardless of length
**Expected Output**: Identical plan content in context as stored in feature.plan

## 2. Edge Cases

### 2.1 Empty/Null Inputs
- **Empty plan string**: feature.plan = ""
- **Whitespace-only plan**: feature.plan = "   \n\t   "
- **Null plan**: feature.plan = None
- **Missing plan property**: feature object lacks plan attribute

### 2.2 Boundary Conditions
- **Very long plans**: Plans exceeding typical prompt limits
- **Plans with special characters**: Unicode, markdown syntax, code blocks
- **Plans with template syntax**: Content containing {variable} patterns
- **Malformed JSON in plans**: Invalid JSON structures within plan text

### 2.3 Invalid States
- **Corrupted feature object**: Partially loaded or damaged feature data
- **Template missing {previous_plan}**: Template without placeholder
- **Template file missing**: plan-headless.md not found
- **Permission errors**: Unable to read template or feature files

### 2.4 Concurrent Operations
- **Plan modification during re-planning**: Feature.plan changed while processing
- **Multiple re-planning attempts**: Rapid successive plan review failures
- **Template updates during processing**: Template file modified mid-execution

### 2.5 Error Conditions
- **Template rendering failure**: Malformed template syntax
- **Context building errors**: Exception during previous_plan_context creation
- **Memory limitations**: Extremely large plans causing memory issues
- **Encoding problems**: Non-UTF8 characters in plan content

## 3. What Constitutes Failure

### 3.1 Critical Failures
- Previous plan context not included when feature.plan exists and is non-empty
- Previous plan context included when it shouldn't be (empty/null plan)
- Template {previous_plan} placeholder not substituted
- Prompt building throws exception due to context handling
- Original plan content modified or corrupted during context creation

### 3.2 Expected Error Behaviors
- **Template missing**: Graceful fallback to basic prompt without template
- **Large plans**: Warning logged but processing continues with truncation
- **Encoding errors**: Invalid characters replaced with safe alternatives
- **Permission errors**: Clear error message indicating file access issues

### 3.3 Rollback Requirements
- Context creation failure should not prevent planning from proceeding
- Template substitution errors should fall back to template without {previous_plan}
- System should never crash due to previous plan context issues

## 4. Out of Scope

### 4.1 UI and Visual Elements
- How previous plan context appears in web UI
- Visual formatting of plan content in browser
- Mobile responsiveness of plan display
- Color coding or syntax highlighting

### 4.2 Performance Benchmarks
- Specific timing requirements for context building
- Memory usage optimization for large plans
- Template rendering performance metrics
- Database query optimization

### 4.3 AI Model Behavior
- Quality of AI-generated plan refinements
- Specific improvements in plan iteration
- AI's understanding of previous plan context
- Generated plan content validation

### 4.4 Integration Dependencies
- Changes to other planning phases
- Modifications to review system behavior
- Updates to feature lifecycle management
- Database schema changes

### 4.5 Configuration and Deployment
- Environment-specific template variations
- Configuration file updates for new feature
- Deployment rollback procedures
- Feature flag management

### 4.6 Security and Authorization
- Access control for plan content
- Content sanitization for XSS prevention
- Audit logging of plan modifications
- User permission validation

This test specification focuses on verifying the core functionality of preserving and utilizing previous plan content during re-planning operations, ensuring robust handling of edge cases while maintaining system stability.

impl_reviews.summary: Core implementation in phases.py and plan-headless.md is correct and follows existing patterns. However, plan-bug.md is missing the {previous_plan} placeholder so bug-type features silently lose previous plan context during re-planning. Additionally, no tests were written despite a detailed test spec requiring coverage of 6 behaviors.
impl_reviews.feedback:
Two issues require fixing:

plan-bug.md missing {previous_plan} placeholder (pipeline/prompts/plan-bug.md): The implementation passes {previous_plan} to _build_prompt() for ALL feature types, but plan-bug.md does not contain the {previous_plan} placeholder. Since _build_prompt uses simple string replacement, the context is silently dropped when item_type == 'bug'. Fix: add {previous_plan} to plan-bug.md in the same position as plan-headless.md (after the description line, before the instructions).

No tests written: The test spec defines 6 behaviors to verify (1.1-1.6) plus edge cases (2.1-2.5), but no test file was created (confirmed: no test_preserve_plan*.py exists). At minimum, tests should cover:
   - Previous plan context is injected when feature.plan is non-empty (1.1)
   - No context added when feature.plan is None/empty/whitespace-only (1.2, edge cases 2.1)
   - Template variable {previous_plan} is substituted correctly (1.3)
   - Prompt building order: template + questions_context + feedback_context (1.4)
   - Plans with special characters or template-like syntax e.g. {variable} patterns in plan content (2.2) - note: since _build_prompt substitutes all keys in the replacements dict via str.replace, a plan containing text matching another template key (e.g. {title}) would cause double-substitution. This is a latent bug worth a regression test.

impl_reviews.summary: Implementation correctly adds {previous_plan} placeholder to both plan-headless.md and plan-bug.md templates, builds previous_plan_context in run_planning using the same established pattern as questions_context/feedback_context, and passes it via _build_prompt substitution. All 11 tests pass, covering context injection, empty/null/whitespace handling, template substitution, prompt ordering, and special characters.

test_results.feedback: All 11 tests pass. Coverage verified for: previous plan context injection, empty/null/whitespace handling, template variable substitution (plan-headless.md and plan-bug.md), prompt building order, and special character preservation (template-like syntax, markdown, unicode). All required behaviors from test spec section 1 are covered except 1.5 (re-planning trigger integration) which requires integration testing.
